subject: Tell the Biden Administration to evacuate U.S. citizens from Lebanon!
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JUSTICE DEMOCRATS
body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter, Israel’s invasion of
Lebanon is worsening by the day.

Last week, the Israeli military launched airstrikes in the heart of Beirut
that leveled a building, killed at least 22 people, and injured over 100.
At the same time in southern Lebanon, an Israeli tank deliberately fired
at United Nations peacekeepers, injuring at least two. They’ve attacked
this UN watchtower several times since, including firing on peacekeepers
in the past 24 hours and using chemical weapons.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/signup/petition-20241017-lebanon/?source=em20241017-36076&akid=36076%2E1203867%2E60vBWX ]Tweet by Human Rights Watch: The Israeli military has carried out
repeated attacks harming United Nations peacekeeping operations in
southwestern Lebanon in apparent violation of the laws of war. Israeli
forces should cease unlawful attacks.

More than 37 Lebanese hospitals have had to close after dozens of medical
staff were killed by Israeli strikes, according to the World Health
Organization. And just yesterday, Israel’s military wiped out an entire
residential village on camera.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/signup/petition-20241017-lebanon/?source=em20241017-36076&akid=36076%2E1203867%2E60vBWX ]Tweet by Mehdi Hasan: Imagine if Russia blew up an entire village in
Ukraine. Imagine what Miller would be saying. And then listen to what he
says when Israel does it. Pathetic. Shameful. Immoral. Tweet by Assal Rad:
Matt Lee: Israel blew up an entire village in southern Lebanon. Miller: I
cannot speak to what their intent was. Lee: Blowing up an entire village
seems to be pretty self revelatory...

Israel is carrying out war crimes and an invasion against a sovereign
nation, Peter.

As the Israeli military’s aggression worsens, U.S. citizens in Lebanon are
being left with few options to escape, with airline ticket prices
skyrocketing into thousands or even tens of thousands of dollars. While
the U.S. Department of State has advised its citizens to leave Lebanon for
their safety, it is not doing enough to evacuate or stop Israel’s
indiscriminate attacks against them.

Dr. Kamel Ahmad Jawad, a U.S. resident from Rep. Rashida Tlaib’s district
of Dearborn, MI was recently killed by Israeli forces while bravely trying
to save lives.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/signup/petition-20241017-lebanon/?source=em20241017-36076&akid=36076%2E1203867%2E60vBWX ]We need the Biden Administration to do everything in its power to
evacuate ALL U.S. citizens in Lebanon immediately: if you agree, add your
name to our petition now.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/signup/petition-20241017-lebanon/?source=em20241017-36076&akid=36076%2E1203867%2E60vBWX ]Add Your Name

As we continue to demand our government stop enabling Israel’s genocide of
Gaza and indiscriminate attacks on civilians in Lebanon, the Biden
Administration must do a better job at protecting and evacuating its
citizens from these war zones.

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats

Dear Peter,

We thought you may be interested to receive this conservative news alert from Illinois Review, the largest conservative media source in Illinois, and the only source in Illinois that has been shared by President Donald Trump.
Mayor Rudy Giuliani Headlines The Conservative Caucus’ 50th Anniversary in DC, Discusses DOJ Double Standard, Prosecuting Political Enemies (https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2024/10/mayor-rudy-giuliani-headlines-the-conservative-caucus-50th-anniversary-in-dc-discusses-doj-double-standard-prosecuting-political-enemies.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=d847b937c6-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D)

Mayor Rudy Giuliani at The Conservative Caucus' 50th Anniversary on Oct. 13. (Illinois Review)
By Illinois Review

Over the weekend, America’s Mayor – Mayor Rudy Giuliani headlined a fundraiser to celebrate The Conservative Caucus’ 50th anniversary as the sold out crowd packed a ballroom at the Lansdowne Resort – just outside of Washington, DC.

TCC – the leading grassroots conservative network in the country, has accelerated its national fundraising efforts since the Spring and is directing resources into key swing states ahead of the November election. TCC President Jim Pfaff – a Capitol Hill veteran and nationally-recognized grassroots leader, served as the evening’s master of ceremonies. Guest speakers included honorary board chairman Barry Goldwater Jr., board chairman Peter Thomas, the gala’s title sponsor Justin Malkin and the 107th Mayor of New York City Rudy Giuliani. There was also a special video greeting from actor and singer Pat Boone and retired U.S. Rep. Steve Stockman congratulating The Conservative Caucus for such a historic milestone.

TCC was founded in 1974 by conservative icon Howard Phillips, who passed away in 2013. Phillips’ widow Peggy and their family were in attendance, including their son Doug and his grandsons Josh and Isaac. At the end of the program, TCC President Jim Pfaff and TCC board chairman Peter Thomas presented Peggy with a special award to pay tribute to Howard’s legacy and life’s work on behalf of the conservative movement.

CLICK TO READ FULL ARTICLE (https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2024/10/mayor-rudy-giuliani-headlines-the-conservative-caucus-50th-anniversary-in-dc-discusses-doj-double-standard-prosecuting-political-enemies.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=d847b937c6-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D)
https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2024/10/mayor-rudy-giuliani-headlines-the-conservative-caucus-50th-anniversary-in-dc-discusses-doj-double-standard-prosecuting-political-enemies.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=d847b937c6-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D
IR’s Mark Vargas, who also works with TCC, speaks on stage during the gala on Oct. 13. (Illinois Review)
During his remarks, Mayor Giuliani discussed lawfare and the Department of Justice’s “double standard” when it came to the investigation of foreign contributions to the Biden family, including his brother Jim Biden and son Hunter Biden, who were paid millions from Ukraine, China and other countries while Joe Biden was serving as vice president.

“The influence peddling was corrupt and should have been prosecuted. I have known Joe Biden for 30 years and I know him to be one of the least intelligent Senators or President ever – and it’s a feeling shared by his law school classmates at Syracuse Law School where he was guilty of plagiarism,” said Mayor Giuliani.

“As a US Attorney I met Biden and was unimpressed too. The FBI and DOJ’s use of lawfare is a threat to the constitution. Armed SWAT teams for Peter Navarro and Trump for Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) and civil contempt charges are far beyond what is typically used for violent criminals,” said Giuliani. “Navarro was placed in leg shackles. And this lawfare against Trump is unprecedented and a threat to our constitution.”
CLICK TO READ FULL ARTICLE (https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2024/10/mayor-rudy-giuliani-headlines-the-conservative-caucus-50th-anniversary-in-dc-discusses-doj-double-standard-prosecuting-political-enemies.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=d847b937c6-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D)
https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2024/10/mayor-rudy-giuliani-headlines-the-conservative-caucus-50th-anniversary-in-dc-discusses-doj-double-standard-prosecuting-political-enemies.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=d847b937c6-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D
IR’s general counsel Scott Kaspar smoking a cigar with Mayor Giuliani after the gala. (Illinois Review)
Other special guests included former NRA president David Keene (https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2023/05/keene-gun-control-is-not-the-panacea-democrats-expect.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=d847b937c6-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D) – a longtime friend of Howard Phillips; George and Simona Papadopoulos (https://x.com/GeorgePapa19?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=d847b937c6-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D) ; a local Virginia Moms for Liberty Chapter; Debbie Doody; Elizabeth Gorman and Illinois Review general counsel Scott Kaspar.

Each guest received an advanced copy of Mayor Giuliani’s latest book, The Biden Crime Family, which will be released on Oct. 29.

clean_body: I’m humbly asking for you to think about what kind of world you want to live in come November 6th | | | | | | I apologize for the late hour, but I’ve been campaigning all day and just found time to sit down and get you this urgent message. Peter, our race against radical liberal Shomari Figures will be decided in the next 24 hours. Our October Mid-Month fundraising deadline is comingTONIGHT @ MIDNIGHT. Simply put: If we don’t raise$3,670before the cutoff,Shomari Figures and the Democrats are going to pull away. Usually, I like to be pretty optimistic – but this close to Election Day there’s no time to mince words. We’re now less than 3 weeks away from our election. If we come up short tonight, there is no more time to make up ground – this is it. A mid-month deadline for an Alabama Congressional Race might sound like small potatoes compared to some of the other emails in your inbox. But if Republicans let the Democrats take AL-02, it’s going to open the floodgates, allowing liberal ideology to seep its way into the Alabama way of life we all know and love. So with that in mind, I’m humbly asking you to spare some of your hard-earned paycheck and put it towards my campaign for Congress. | | | | | My very best, Caroleene Dobson | | | | Republican nominee for U.S. CongressAL-02 | | | | | | | | Caroleene Dobson is a distinguished attorney, wife, mother, District Two resident, and a lifelong advocate for conservative values. Born and raised in Beatrice, Alabama, Dobson grew up on her family's fifth-generation cattle farm, where she learned the meaning of hard work and developed a firsthand understanding of the challenges faced by hardworking families and entrepreneurs. Currently practicing real estate law at the Maynard Nexsen law firm, Dobson represents a diverse clientele, including homebuilders, retailers, small business owners, and private landowners. She has spent her career advocating for her client’s interests while also achieving tangible, positive outcomes. In Congress, she will hold true to her core conservative values while ensuring Washington D.C. is working for the people of District Two. A passionate advocate for families, farms, and faith, Dobson aims to preserve the bedrock values and moral backbone that have defined our nation. With a call for Alabama common sense, she is determined to challenge the far-left agenda in Washington, D.C., advocating for the rights of property owners and defending the freedom to think, speak, and act without interference. Caroleene, alongside her husband Bobby, is the proud parent of two daughters, Philippa and Lydia. name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
subject: This is personal to me
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
Did you know that over half of all Members of Congress are millionaires? Meanwhile, the median household income is only $70,784. 👈🏽 **This is wild.**
Many of our lawmakers have no lived experience of working paycheck to paycheck or trying to pay rent working a low-wage job.
To me, policy is personal. When I worked as a bartender, I relied on tips to pay the bills. I know the urgent and daily stresses of working class people because I have lived them. And I intimately understand how important measures like raising the minimum wage, universal health care, universal child care, and free college can be for families living in financial uncertainty.
That’s why I’m in Congress: **to represent working families like mine.**
I am honored to be here, and I can’t do this work without you — the grassroots supporters who have had my back every step of the way. I can’t self-fund my campaign by writing a big check, and I don’t do any donor call-time or exclusive fundraising events.

Many of our lawmakers have no lived experience of working paycheck to paycheck or trying to pay rent working a low-wage job. To me, policy is personal. When I worked as a bartender, I relied on tips to pay the bills. I know the urgent and daily stresses of working class people because I have lived them. And I intimately understand how important measures like raising the minimum wage, universal health care, universal child care, and free college can be for families living in financial uncertainty. That’s why I’m in Congress: to represent working families like mine. I am honored to be here, and I can’t do this work without you — the grassroots supporters who have had my back every step of the way. I can’t self-fund my campaign by writing a big check, and I don’t do any donor call-time or exclusive fundraising events. ** Yours in service, Alexandria | ---|--- | | ---|---|--- Email us: mailto: speak@ocasiocortez.com

After an Israeli strike hit an encampment of displaced families on the

longer.

letting the Israeli government get away with these horrors.

"**Texas judge says state can't execute Robert Roberson, but attorney general plans to swiftly appeal** ," Texas Tribune's **Kayla Guo** -- "As Texas prison officials ready the death chamber to execute**Robert Roberson** on Thursday night, legal battles aimed at delaying his death continue to play out amid a thundering chorus of people who believe the state is about to kill an innocent man and hope last-minute measures will buy him more time.

On Thursday afternoon, a state district court judge in Travis County ruled that the state doesn't have the authority to execute Roberson if it prevents him from complying with a last-minute legislative subpoena. But the Texas Department of Criminal Justice said the attorney general's office plans to appeal the ruling to the state's highest criminal court, which has repeatedly shot down efforts to halt Roberson's execution.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $7/mo](https://substack.com/redirect/50c3bcd7-f71f-40a8-b044-01086a4a3c3c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
That judge's ruling**** was in reaction to a Texas House committee's [stunning decision Wednesday to subpoena Roberson](https://substack.com/redirect/b4195f14-437f-42f7-949d-a47a4de71643?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ahead of his Thursday execution, a step that sought to give the man a final lifeline after a series of court rejections left him on track to become the first person in the country executed for allegedly shaking a baby to death.

Roberson was convicted of killing his 2-year-old daughter, who was diagnosed with shaken baby syndrome. But experts, lawmakers and the lead detective in the girl's case say the science supporting Roberson's death sentence no longer holds up -- and the state's "junk science" law should have already halted his execution.

The subpoena "sets up a bit of a separation of powers issue," Benjamin Wolff, director of the Texas Office of Capital and Forensic Writs, said on Wednesday, adding that he had not seen this maneuver attempted before, so it was not clear what could happen. "It's an unprecedented subpoena and an unprecedented case."
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $70/yr](https://substack.com/redirect/50c3bcd7-f71f-40a8-b044-01086a4a3c3c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
But at 5 p.m., an hour before Roberson's scheduled execution, it was unclear if that gambit would work. It could be his last chance, unless Gov. **Greg Abbott** steps in. The U.S. Supreme Court on Thursday afternoon declined to stop the execution, though Justice **Sonia Sotomayor** urged Abbott to issue a 30-day reprieve.

"That could prevent a miscarriage of justice from occurring: executing a man who has raised credible evidence of actual innocence," she wrote.
The Texas House Criminal Jurisprudence Committee approved its subpoena hours after the state's highest criminal court again declined to stop the execution, and after the Texas Board of Pardons and Parole denied Roberson's request for clemency. Gov. Greg Abbott cannot defy the board's recommendation, but he can issue a 30-day reprieve. Abbott has remained silent. Roberson's lawyers also filed last-minute attempts to halt the execution with a state district court, the state's highest criminal court and the U.S. Supreme Court.

In a Wednesday evening [filing](https://substack.com/redirect/dae9091e-7fec-43b5-815f-1141234995b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with the high court, **Craig W. Cosper** , an assistant state attorney general, argues that Roberson's appeal is "unworthy of the Court's attention" and that there is no "compelling reason" to review the case.

Roberson's attorneys [responded](https://substack.com/redirect/792b7432-6bc4-42e4-b99b-db8135218efa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the man was denied due process and that the state relies on "a litany of lies."" ($5/mo or $50/yr or $199 lifetime) TOP NEWS "Texas judge says state can't execute Robert Roberson, but attorney general plans to swiftly appeal ," Texas Tribune's Kayla Guo -- "As Texas prison officials ready the death chamber to executeRobert Roberson on Thursday night, legal battles aimed at delaying his death continue to play out amid a thundering chorus of people who believe the state is about to kill an innocent man and hope last-minute measures will buy him more time. On Thursday afternoon, a state district court judge in Travis County ruled that the state doesn't have the authority to execute Roberson if it prevents him from complying with a last-minute legislative subpoena. But the Texas Department of Criminal Justice said the attorney general's office plans to appeal the ruling to the state's highest criminal court, which has repeatedly shot down efforts to halt Roberson's execution. That judge's ruling** was in reaction to a Texas House committee's ahead of his Thursday execution, a step that sought to give the man a final lifeline after a series of court rejections left him on track to become the first person in the country executed for allegedly shaking a baby to death. Roberson was convicted of killing his 2-year-old daughter, who was diagnosed with shaken baby syndrome. But experts, lawmakers and the lead detective in the girl's case say the science supporting Roberson's death sentence no longer holds up -- and the state's "junk science" law should have already halted his execution. The subpoena "sets up a bit of a separation of powers issue," Benjamin Wolff, director of the Texas Office of Capital and Forensic Writs, said on Wednesday, adding that he had not seen this maneuver attempted before, so it was not clear what could happen. "It's an unprecedented subpoena and an unprecedented case." But at 5 p.m., an hour before Roberson's scheduled execution, it was unclear if that gambit would work. It could be his last chance, unless Gov. Greg Abbott steps in. The U.S. Supreme Court on Thursday afternoon declined to stop the execution, though Justice Sonia Sotomayor urged Abbott to issue a 30-day reprieve. "That could prevent a miscarriage of justice from occurring: executing a man who has raised credible evidence of actual innocence," she wrote. The Texas House Criminal Jurisprudence Committee approved its subpoena hours after the state's highest criminal court again declined to stop the execution, and after the Texas Board of Pardons and Parole denied Roberson's request for clemency. Gov. Greg Abbott cannot defy the board's recommendation, but he can issue a 30-day reprieve. Abbott has remained silent. Roberson's lawyers also filed last-minute attempts to halt the execution with a state district court, the state's highest criminal court and the U.S. Supreme Court. In a Wednesday evening with the high court, Craig W. Cosper , an assistant state attorney general, argues that Roberson's appeal is "unworthy of the Court's attention" and that there is no "compelling reason" to review the case. Roberson's attorneys that the man was denied due process and that the state relies on "a litany of lies.""
